newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST-Preview of RBNZ economic projections.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Preview of RBNZ economic projections.

text.p: Following is a survey of economists' forecasts for Treasury's Pre-Election Economic and Fiscal Update on Thursday and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's economic projections on Friday.
GROWTH FORECAST AND GOVERNMENT OPERATING SURPLUS

We asked economists to state their own forecasts for growth in production-based Gross Domestic Product (March quarter to March quarter) for 1996-97 and 1997-98, and their own forecast for the government's operating surplus for the 1995-96 and 1996-97 June years.
UNDERLYING INFLATION, TWI AND 90-DAY BILLS ASSUMPTIONS

We asked economists to state their own forecasts for March quarter to March quarter percentage change in underlying inflation for 1996-97 and 1997-8; the underlying inflation rate the Reserve Bank will forecast for the September quarter; the bank's technical assumption for 90-day bank bill rates over its forecast period; the rate of appreciation the bank will assume in the New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index, and the starting
point it will take for the index.
* National Bank said it expected the Reserve Bank to asusme 90-day bill rates around 10 percent to mid-1997, declining thereafter
We asked economists whether they expected the Reserve Bank to ease in its September 13 statement, and in what month they did expect an easing to occur.

None of the 10 economists expected an easing in Friday's statement. Bank of New Zealand Treasury Economist Peter Jolly qualified that by saying although he did not expect an explicit easing, the central bank would seek a "rebalancing" from current conditions that were tighter than required.

On the timing of an easing, Bancorp Treasury Services Executive Director Roger Kerr said: "We expect easing to occur late October by the market easing conditions itself, and the RBNZ sanctioning the easing by not commenting."
Westpac and Bankers Trust saw a November/December easing.
ASB, Garlick and Co, National Bank and SBC Warburg all opted for December.
First NZ Capital picked January 1997, while ANZ said it was looking for an easing in the first quarter of 1997.
